instagram_caption:
A 200 megapixel phone camera usually saves a 12 megapixel photo.

By default, Samsung's Galaxy S23 Ultra merges up to 16 tiny pixels into one bigger one, a trick called pixel binning, and saves a 12MP image (TechRadar). Bigger pixels catch more light, so night shots come out brighter and less grainy (Android Authority).

TechRadar also compared two phones with the same 108MP count and found the photos were not even close: the one with the larger sensor won.

The lesson: megapixels tell you how much, not how good. Look at sensor size first.

Source: TechRadar, Android Authority, How-To Geek.
